chapter: Ben Webster, Tatum and Los Angeles scene
title: Art Tatum's encouragement and Slam Stewart
summary: Tatum took him around and told him to be himself; he describes Tatum's handicap, forming of the trio with Slam Stewart and Tiny Grimes.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: And Tatum did the same thing. Tatum liked me, and he used to take me around. He used to have his chauffeur come pick me up where I was working, and then we'd come and we'd get Art, and then we'd go out and play all night. That's where I overcame my fear of playing in front of someone who was exceptionally much greater than I am. He just told me, he just said, "Just play what you play. Play... Be yourself. Play." He says, "I like it. I don't care who else likes it. Play! If you don't play, I will play." He said, "Hurry up, sit down."
He'd show me all kinds of things. Art!...oh, he was marvelous. Yeah, Art was somethin' else. He made a record for me, "Ooh, Would You Like To Take A Walk?" -- he did that for me.
Yeah, I always liked that song.
Art was able to get around pretty well with his handicap.

Oh yeah. You should have seen him... Did you ever see Art pour a beer? He'd hold the bottle up in front of his eye real close, like this, and he'd take a glass, and he could see it. It was fuzzy, but he could see. He knew what it was at the top. Then he put the bottle down, and he knew right where the straight shot was, and he'd grab that double straight shot, and WHUP, and then go down a beer. Then he'd sit down and rip off "In The Still Of The Night" in five sharps, so fast you couldn't even beat your foot to it.

I was there the first night he heard Slam Stewart. He decided to form his trio. Slam Stewart was the first bass player he had ever played that could talk with him, anticipate him and all that. He said, "Now there is my bass player. I've finally found a bass player. I'm going to form a trio now." Where he got Tiny Grimes, boy, I don't know...
Neither does Tiny. He said, "I don't know why he got me," because Tiny had such a hard time, you know, keeping up with him.
He complained that they never rehearsed or anything, and he had to get up there and try to follow him. But I don't know, he must have liked him.
I guess so. I don't know...

Well, Tiny said something funny when I interviewed him once. He said, 'It was an honor to play with Mr. Tatum, but it was not a pleasure.' I mean, that was as far as he was concerned. Whereas Slam, of course, he continued to work with him on ...(?)...
Yeah, the difference between all the other bass players that played with Art and Slam is... There's no comparison.
Slam had a great ear, and then of course, he studied violin before he played bass and he had all that knowledge of harmony.
